items.title: Why early-stage delinquency is the cheapest recovery window
items.summary: Accounts that slip 1 to 30 days past due respond far better to a respectful reminder than accounts left to age. Learn how a structured early-bucket process protects both your portfolio and the customer relationship.
points: Segment accounts by days-past-due, not just by amount
Use a clear, polite first contact within 48 hours of default
Offer a documented repayment path before escalation
Track promise-to-pay vs actual payment to refine outreach

items.title: Your rights when a lender or recovery agent contacts you
items.summary: Recovery must be lawful and respectful. Know what is acceptable, what is not, and how to raise a concern with the lender's grievance officer or the RBI ombudsman.
points: Calls should be made only during reasonable hours
Agents must identify themselves and the lender they represent
Harassment, threats or public shaming are not acceptable
Every lender must have a grievance redressal process

items.title: Fair-practice recovery: what good looks like
items.summary: A compliant recovery operation has trained agents, call recording where required, clear scripts, escalation matrices and audit trails. Here is a practical checklist for lenders reviewing their recovery partners.
points: Documented agent code of conduct and training records
Call and visit logs retained for audit
Complaint handling with defined turnaround times
Regular partner audits and mystery-shopping

items.title: One-time settlement (OTS): is it right for you?
items.summary: An OTS can close an old loan for less than the full dues, but it can also affect your credit report. Understand the trade-offs before you agree, and always get the settlement terms in writing.
points: Ask for the complete outstanding statement first
Get the settlement amount and closure terms in writing
Pay only through traceable channels to the lender's account
Request a No-Dues / closure letter after payment

items.title: Skip tracing and field verification for old accounts
items.summary: When a borrower has moved or changed numbers, tracing becomes the bottleneck. A mix of data validation, digital tracing and on-ground verification reconnects accounts that look lost.
points: Validate contact data before spending on field visits
Prioritise by recoverable value and traceability score
Use geo-tagged, time-stamped field reports
Close the loop by updating the borrower record

items.title: How EMI is calculated (and how tenure changes your interest)
items.summary: A longer tenure lowers your monthly instalment but increases the total interest paid. Use our calculators on this page to compare plans side by side before you restructure.
points: EMI depends on principal, rate and tenure
Longer tenure = lower EMI but higher total interest
Part-prepayments cut interest the most early in the loan
Compare options with the restructuring calculator

items.title: Documents to keep ready for a loan resolution discussion
items.summary: Having your paperwork organised speeds up any resolution. From the sanction letter to repayment history, this is the short list worth gathering before you speak to a lender or advisor.
points: Loan agreement and sanction letter
Latest statement of account
Past communication and notices received
Proof of income and current financial position

items.title: Data privacy in recovery operations
items.summary: Borrower data is sensitive. Secure handling, role-based access and strict purpose limitation are not optional for any partner working with your portfolio.
points: Share only the fields needed for the task
Encrypt data in transit and at rest
Role-based access with activity logs
Delete or return data when the mandate ends
